developer.note: Q8_0 + MTP. Q4_K_M (qwen3.8:27b) is the comparison arm — quantization damage on a 27B lands hardest on instruction-following under long context, which is what containment and section-lint depend on. num_ctx here is PI's window — what the agent may fill before it must compact — not the server's. The contained worker honours it because the controller writes the models.json pi reads; the loaded model's own context comes from OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH and is a property of the running server, which pi cannot set. Expect /api/ps to report a different and usually larger number, and do not read that as drift. Raised from 32768 to 65536 on 2026-09-15: the old figure was inherited from the co-residency probe, where it was the most that fit beside the judge, and the regime is serial. Measured consequence of the old number, once the contained worker started honouring it — a single spec session COMPACTED TWICE, which means it lost the earlier part of its own reasoning mid-task. Raise again if sessions still compact. MEASURED 2026-09-17, which closes the question of whether pi keeps a context the controller loads: it does not. ollama's journal on bean-002 shows the preload at 17:24:02 (n_ctx_slot = 65536) and a reload eight seconds later at 17:24:10 (n_ctx_slot = 262144), and every request of that session ran at 262144. pi speaks the openai-completions API, which has no field for the server-side context, so nothing inside a session can hold it. ensure-loaded.sh still preloads — it keeps the weights resident and reports honestly what the server granted — but the hold does not survive pi's first request. The only real fix is OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH on the server, which is one number for every role and every other project on this machine, so it is the operator's call. Recorded per step as conditions.server_ctx_honoured, which is its own field precisely so that a context the controller cannot hold does not make declared_matches_observed false on every run.

judge.note: Different family from the developer by design. thinking was `high` until 2026-09-14, when it was measured to produce NO OUTPUT AT ALL: thinking tokens and content tokens share num_predict, and at high this model spends the entire budget reasoning and emits empty content. It was `medium` until 2026-09-16, when two measurements agreed it should be `low`. (1) bench/format-support.sh against a REAL 18KB payload rather than a short probe: gpt-oss:120b holds the judgement schema at `low` and, at `medium` and `high`, spends its whole budget thinking and writes nothing. `low` is the only eligible configuration on this box. (2) bench/judge-fitness.sh, three passes at each level, same six cases: at `medium` 2 of 15 named and 2 false accepts, with the clean control rejected outright in two passes; at `low` 4 named and 1 false accept, and the control never confidently rejected. Better on the number that matters and on the control. It is NOT reproducible at either level — five of six cases gave more than one verdict across three identical passes at `low` — so this is a better setting for a judge that still cannot be a gate, and the advisory decision stands. Cost: more cases cut off by the token budget at `low` (4 of 18 vs 2 of 18), because less of the budget goes to thinking and more to a longer answer. JUDGE_NUM_PREDICT is the knob for that and is deliberately NOT changed in the same commit, so the next comparison has one variable.

smoke.note: Cheap stand-in for the judge while iterating on skill text, where loop speed matters more than verdict quality. Never used for a run whose telemetry is kept.

_known_gaps: pr is bound to developer because the forked pipeline-pr skill still composes the PR body itself. Spec §06 stage 11 makes push/PR pure controller work with no model at all — the pre-PR audit already drafts the body. Fix when the controller lands.

num_ctx is an intent, not a lever: pi exposes no context flag, so Ollama serves what OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH or the last request set. run-step.sh no longer stamps this number as fact -- conditions.num_ctx is read from /api/ps and this value is recorded under conditions.declared with a declared_matches_observed flag. Control still has to come from the unit (a single global value, so it cannot express a per-role context): spec §09 healthcheck.
_step_roles_note: step_roles binds a run-step.sh step to a role. Audits are not in this table and never were routed by it in the live line: orchestrate.sh runs judge.sh, which reads .roles.judge directly, and run-step.sh now refuses an audit-* step name. Four entries here pointed at a code path that was measured not to work (a pi session reaching for a repo_browser namespace that does not exist and answering anyway); they were removed 2026-09-16 together with that path. The judge is bound in judge.sh, not here. `implement` went at the same time: factory-implement was deleted days earlier and run-step has had no branch for it since, so the entry routed a step name that is now an error.
